clue.text: Rugger player quietly brings about scrum, OK?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the soft-music sign, so 'about' signals a container here
a scrum is a jumbled heap of bodies, so it tells us to jumble the letters of the words beside it

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical direction for playing quietly

explanation.surface: A rugby commentator checks that a player is gently easing his way around the scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrum' looks like part of the rugby picture but is the anagram signal, and 'about' is the container signal. A Springbok is a member of South Africa's national rugby union team.
explanation.definitionFit: The Springboks are South Africa's national rugby side, so any one of their team is a rugby player.

clue.text: Printer's type confused smug newspaper boss

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is slang for sanctimonious or smug
ED is the usual short form of editor, the person in charge of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied editor gets his printing type in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie (or pi) is printers' slang for type that has been spilled and mixed up; type in that state is called pied.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, type that has been jumbled out of order is described as pied.

clue.text: Freely enjoy eluding order

indicators.note: putting the letters of the word beside it in a new order is the signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Someone happily indulges themselves by dodging the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a noun meaning a command being dodged, but it tells you to reorder the letters of ELUDING.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge is to allow yourself a pleasure without holding back, which is enjoying something freely.

clue.text: A millstone for the poor street organist

explanation.walkthrough: An organ-grinder turned the handle of a barrel organ for coins, so the poor street musician is the grinder of the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: One stone that crushes grain is a grinder, and an organ-grinder is a busker who cranks a barrel organ in the street.

clue.text: To turn us in or turn us out?

definitions.note: the definition includes 'us': the answer is the verb that means to turn out, applied to us

indicators.note: the clue tells us to put 'us' in the reversed word, so 'in' is the container signal
to turn a word round is to read it backwards, applied here to the opening word

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone will hand us over to the police or simply throw us out.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper print shows 'Te', a misreading of 'To'. 'turn' reverses that word to OT, and 'in' puts the pronoun inside it. The definition reuses 'us': to oust us is to turn us out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or expel someone from a place is to oust them, so ousting us means throwing us out.

clue.text: Go to the opposite side of the chamber

definitions.text: Go to the opposite side of the chamber

parts.words: Go to the opposite side of the chamber
parts.note: read as a parliamentary phrase: an MP who moves from his party's benches to sit with the other side of the House has defected

explanation.walkthrough: The chamber is the House of Commons, where government and opposition benches face each other across the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: In the House of Commons, an MP who changes party literally walks over to the benches facing them.

clue.text: An Italian get-together that sets tongues wagging

definitions.text: An Italian get-together that sets tongues wagging

parts.words: An Italian get-together that sets tongues wagging
parts.note: describes a social gathering with an Italian name whose purpose is talk, since its name means conversation

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for a social evening devoted to conversation, especially on literary or artistic topics.

clue.text: An unprompted confession that one got in without paying?

definitions.text: that one got in without paying

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'admission' as owning up; the second takes it as being allowed in, as at a museum with no entry fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A confession given freely is a free admission, while entry with no charge is also free admission.

clue.text: Demonstrate over the house? Worth looking into

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer, a place that is worth visiting and looking round

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, or on top of, the second

parts.note: to demonstrate something is to show it
a place can mean a house, as in 'come back to my place'

explanation.surface: An estate agent shows a client around a house that deserves a closer look.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits on top of the second. The definition is descriptive: a showplace is somewhere visitors go to look round.
explanation.definitionFit: A showplace is a building or site visited for its beauty or interest, so it merits a tour.

clue.text: Inferior worker isn't straightforward

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective meaning sly or not open

parts.note: lower in rank, as in an under-gardener
a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand or factory hand

explanation.surface: A junior employee is accused of being devious.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the verb phrase 'isn't straightforward', standing in for the adjective: underhand dealings are not straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealing is sly and deceitful, the opposite of honest and open.

clue.text: But it needn't be one of Cook's failures

definitions.text: But it needn't be one of Cook's failures

parts.words: But it needn't be one of Cook's failures
parts.note: a cook who makes a mess of a dish is said to make a mess of it in a phrase using this word, yet the word is also a perfectly good dish of chopped meat

explanation.walkthrough: To 'make a hash of' something is to botch it, so a hash sounds like a kitchen disaster; in fact it is a recognised dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a hash of something means bungling it, but a hash is also a proper dish of chopped meat and potato.

clue.text: Cutting part of a shoulder

parts.note: read two ways at once: the sharp edge of a knife, and the flat bone of the shoulder

explanation.definitionFit: The sharp edge of a knife or sword is its blade, and the scapula is the shoulder blade.

clue.text: The river reflects an inconstant star

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the star's name is read backwards

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens and then fades, so its light is inconstant

explanation.surface: A star's image is mirrored in the surface of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The print reads 'inconstancy', a misreading of 'inconstant'. 'reflects' turns NOVA round to give the river; there are several River Avons in England, one flowing through Stratford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avon is a well-known English river, the one Shakespeare's Stratford stands on.

clue.text: An early Englishman whose son digested chop

indicators.note: food that is digested is taken inside, so the word for son takes the second piece into it

parts.note: taken as written
AX (the American spelling of axe) means to chop

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon's boy wolfs down a chop of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digested' is the container signal. 'chop' looks like a piece of meat being eaten, but it is the verb, to axe, in its American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxons were Germanic settlers in England from the fifth century, among the earliest English people.

clue.text: Stay clear when hungry prima donna turns up!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Stay clear when hungry prima donna turns up!' (5): DIVA turned up gives AVID (hungry), but no word supplies the O of AVOID; the clue appears garbled or cut in the print
annotationWithheld.clue: Stay clear when hungry prima donna turns up!

clue.text: Steam pioneer taking time, but, with what power!

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer whose improved steam engine powered the Industrial Revolution
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A remark on how slowly the steam engine was developed, but how mighty it proved.
explanation.walkthrough: The unit of power, the watt, is named after James Watt, which ties the surface to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattage is the amount of electrical or mechanical energy used, measured in watts.

clue.text: Don't get into such gear if you want to get on

definitions.text: Don't get into such gear if you want to get on

parts.words: Don't get into such gear if you want to get on
parts.note: advice to a driver: one gear takes the car backwards, so it is no use for moving forwards

explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' reads as succeeding in life, but here it also means moving forwards in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The gear that drives a car backwards is the wrong choice for making forward progress.

clue.text: Be prone to idle about, and admit it

indicators.note: turned about means moved round, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: to own or own up is to admit something

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to confess that they are inclined to laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes LIED from the anagram fodder. 'prone' looks like 'inclined to', but here it means lying face down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prone means lying flat, so to lie down is to take up that position.

clue.text: Has memo about lack of urgency

indicators.note: turned about means moved round, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: a memo is a short note

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles an office memo without any sense of urgency.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an indirect anagram: 'memo' must first become NOTE, then 'about' rearranges HAS and NOTE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in no haste is to take one's time, without any hurry.

clue.text: It gets dished up on special chana

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'It gets dished up on special chana' (7): no reading of these words builds the letters of SPINACH; the print appears garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: It gets dished up on special chana

clue.text: An unidentified VIP?

parts.note: the word for an unnamed person is also a word for a person of importance, as in 'he is really somebody'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an unnamed person, but 'a someone' is also a person of standing.

clue.text: Clot mishandled a pistol

indicators.note: something mishandled is knocked about, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool fumbles with a handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: The print reads 'Got', a misreading of 'Clot'. 'mishandled' rearranges CLOT; a Colt is the American revolver made by Samuel Colt's company.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is a famous make of revolver, named after the gunmaker Samuel Colt.

clue.text: Times said to add a season to food

definitions.note: the herb is used to season food

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the word time, spoken

explanation.surface: A saying that time adds flavour to food.
explanation.walkthrough: The print reads 'Times and', a misreading of 'Time's said'. The herb is pronounced like 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a herb added to food to season it.

clue.text: An important baker in Stoke

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent is the centre of the English pottery industry, where clay is baked hard in ovens

explanation.walkthrough: Stoke-on-Trent in Staffordshire is known as the Potteries; 'baker' suggests bread, but what is baked there is pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The oven in which pottery is fired is the key 'baker' in Stoke-on-Trent, home of the Potteries.

clue.text: Doctrines sect leader put into one written document

indicators.note: the first letter of the sect is placed inside the other two pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MS is the usual abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten document

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A religious group's head is named in a single founding text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes S from 'sect', and 'put into' places it between I and MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Isms are distinctive doctrines or ideologies, named from the suffix in words like communism.

clue.text: Lean on an objection

parts.note: 'but' introduces an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Someone presses an objection on another.
explanation.walkthrough: A building that abuts another leans or rests against it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to adjoin or rest against something, as one wall rests on another.

clue.text: Smith's U-turn

parts.note: a blacksmith's U-shaped product, joined with a word for a curve in a river or road

explanation.walkthrough: The smith is a blacksmith, who shapes horseshoes; a horseshoe is U-shaped, so the U-turn is a horseshoe-shaped bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop in a river or road shaped like a horseshoe, the U-shaped item a smith makes.

clue.text: A filmy torch-bearer who must
